domain.name: Automotive Diagnostics & Maintenance
domain.description: Practical vehicle diagnostics, starting/charging, OBD data, fluids, cooling, tires, brakes, and electrical fundamentals with safety boundaries.

competencies.name: Structured Vehicle Diagnosis
competencies.description: Diagnose symptoms systematically before replacing parts.
competencies.purpose: Reduce guesswork, wasted parts, and missed root causes.

units.title: Symptoms are evidence, not diagnoses
units.content: A no-start, dim light, noise, vibration, warning lamp, or leak can have multiple causes; diagnosis should move from symptom to system to testable cause.

units.title: Vehicle diagnostic loop
units.content: Confirm the complaint; gather operating conditions and recent history; perform a visual/safety inspection; identify affected systems; test the simplest likely causes first; compare results with specifications; then verify the repair or conclusion.

units.title: Diagnostic failures
units.content: Avoid replacing the most common failed part without testing, clearing evidence before recording it, and interpreting one measurement without operating context.

drills.title: Diagnose a no-start complaint
drills.prompt: Build a diagnostic sequence for a vehicle with dim lights, weak power locks, and no crank after a long drive.

competencies.name: Battery, Starting & Charging Systems
competencies.description: Understand the relationship among battery state, connections, starter demand, and alternator output.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose common power and no-start problems safely.

units.title: Voltage, capacity, connection, and charging are different questions
units.content: A battery can show voltage yet lack cranking capacity; poor connections can imitate battery failure; charging problems can leave a good battery discharged.

units.title: Power-system checks
units.content: Inspect terminals and grounds; measure resting voltage; observe voltage under load or crank with appropriate equipment; check charging voltage only when safe and running; compare against vehicle-specific guidance before concluding which component is at fault.

units.title: Power-system failures
units.content: Avoid sparks near batteries, bypassing safety procedures, assuming a jump-start proves the battery is bad, and condemning an alternator from resting battery voltage alone.

drills.title: Analyze a charging-system case
drills.prompt: A car starts after a jump but dies again later. Explain the evidence needed to separate battery, alternator, belt, cable, and parasitic-load possibilities.

competencies.name: OBD Codes & Scan Data
competencies.description: Use diagnostic trouble codes and live data as clues within a broader diagnosis.
competencies.purpose: Interpret electronic evidence without treating codes as part-replacement instructions.

units.title: A code identifies a detected condition, not always the failed part
units.content: Diagnostic trouble codes reflect monitored conditions and system logic; wiring, sensors, mechanical problems, leaks, power supply, or software can produce similar codes.

units.title: Code-driven diagnosis
units.content: Record codes, freeze-frame, readiness, and relevant live data before clearing; research system logic; inspect related basics; test likely causes; then confirm whether the code returns after repair and drive conditions.

units.title: Scan-tool failures
units.content: Avoid parts-cannon diagnosis from code descriptions, clearing codes before saving freeze-frame data, and interpreting sensor values without knowing expected conditions.

drills.title: Interpret a lean-condition code
drills.prompt: Explain how to use freeze-frame and live data to investigate a lean-condition code without assuming the oxygen sensor is bad.

competencies.name: Fluids & Preventive Maintenance
competencies.description: Understand basic fluid roles, inspection, service intervals, and contamination risks.
competencies.purpose: Support reliable operation without mixing incompatible fluids or ignoring leaks.

units.title: Fluid type and condition matter
units.content: Engine oil, coolant, brake fluid, transmission fluid, power-steering fluid, and washer fluid have different specifications and service requirements; wrong fluid can cause damage or safety problems.

units.title: Fluid inspection workflow
units.content: Use vehicle-specific guidance; inspect level and condition only under the correct temperature and operating conditions; identify leaks or contamination; use the specified fluid; document service and recheck after operation.

units.title: Fluid-service failures
units.content: Avoid opening hot pressurized cooling systems, mixing unknown coolant types, overfilling, using generic substitutes without specification, and treating a low level as solved without checking for loss.

drills.title: Build a maintenance review
drills.prompt: Create a safe inspection checklist for a high-mileage vehicle before a long trip.

competencies.name: Cooling System & Overheating Diagnosis
competencies.description: Understand heat removal, coolant circulation, pressure, airflow, and common overheating evidence.
competencies.purpose: Recognize when overheating is unsafe and diagnose without dangerous hot-system handling.

units.title: Overheating can escalate quickly
units.content: Loss of coolant, poor circulation, fan/airflow faults, pressure loss, combustion leakage, and sensor/control problems can overheat an engine; continued driving can create major damage.

units.title: Overheat triage
units.content: Stop operation when temperature or warning conditions indicate danger; allow safe cooling; inspect for visible leaks, belt/fan condition, coolant evidence, and stored codes; only perform pressure or hot-system tests with proper equipment and procedure.

units.title: Cooling-system safety failures
units.content: Never open a hot pressurized cooling system, continue driving a severely overheating engine, or place hands near moving fans or belts during diagnosis.

drills.title: Triage an overheating vehicle
drills.prompt: A vehicle temperature rises at idle but drops while moving. Build a safe diagnostic hypothesis list and test order.

competencies.name: Tires, Steering & Suspension Screening
competencies.description: Recognize common tire wear, pressure, alignment, steering, and suspension clues.
competencies.purpose: Identify safety concerns and guide further inspection.

units.title: Tire wear tells a story
units.content: Pressure, alignment, suspension wear, rotation history, load, and driving conditions can create different wear patterns; one worn tire can indicate a larger chassis problem.

units.title: Tire and front-end screening
units.content: Check cold pressure against vehicle specification, tread depth and pattern, sidewall damage, wheel fastener condition, visible steering/suspension play or leakage, and symptoms such as pull, vibration, or noise; escalate uncertain structural or steering faults.

units.title: Tire and steering failures
units.content: Avoid driving on exposed cords, severe sidewall damage, loose wheels, or obvious steering instability; do not infer alignment correction without checking mechanical wear first.

drills.title: Interpret tire wear
drills.prompt: A vehicle has inner-edge wear on both front tires and steering pull. List likely categories and the safe inspection order.

competencies.name: Brake System Awareness
competencies.description: Understand basic hydraulic and friction braking components and recognize unsafe symptoms.
competencies.purpose: Treat braking faults as safety-critical and know when professional inspection is required.

units.title: Brake feel, noise, and stopping behavior are safety evidence
units.content: Soft pedals, pulling, grinding, warning lights, fluid loss, overheating, or reduced braking can indicate faults that should not be ignored or tested casually on public roads.

units.title: Brake concern screening
units.content: Record symptoms; inspect warning lights and fluid evidence; visually check accessible pad/rotor/tire conditions where safe; avoid road-testing severe faults; refer hydraulic, ABS, structural, or uncertain brake problems to qualified service.

units.title: Brake safety failures
units.content: Do not drive when braking ability is seriously reduced, ignore brake-fluid loss, work under an unsupported vehicle, or assume noise alone identifies the required repair.

drills.title: Screen a brake warning complaint
drills.prompt: A driver reports grinding and longer stopping distance. Describe the safe triage and escalation process.

competencies.name: Vehicle Electrical Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand voltage, grounds, fuses, relays, connectors, and basic circuit testing.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose electrical faults without bypassing circuit protection or damaging modules.

units.title: A circuit needs source, path, load, and return
units.content: Open circuits, high resistance, short circuits, poor grounds, damaged connectors, incorrect fuses, and module control can all interrupt electrical function.

units.title: Basic circuit diagnosis
units.content: Consult the correct diagram; verify power supply and fuse rating; test for voltage and ground at appropriate points; use voltage-drop testing for loaded connections where applicable; protect modules and connectors from accidental shorts.

units.title: Electrical-diagnosis failures
units.content: Avoid replacing fuses with higher ratings, probing unknown sensitive circuits carelessly, bypassing relays or safety interlocks without proper procedure, and assuming continuity with the circuit unloaded proves a good connection.

drills.title: Diagnose a dead accessory circuit
drills.prompt: Build a test sequence for an accessory that stopped working while other vehicle systems are normal.
